source: NCERT Class XI, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch. 12 (Water — Oceans).

sections.heading: 1. Hydrological Cycle and Ocean Relief
points: The **water (hydrological) cycle** circulates water between oceans, atmosphere and land (evaporation → condensation → precipitation → runoff).
Oceans cover ~**71%** of the Earth; the largest is the **Pacific**.

sub: **Continental shelf** — shallow, gently sloping edge (rich in fisheries, minerals, oil).
**Deep sea plain (abyssal plain)** — flat, deep ocean floor (largest).

points: Minor features: ridges, seamounts, guyots, canyons, atolls.

sections.heading: 2. Temperature of Ocean Water
points: Sea surface temperature decreases from the **equator to the poles**, and with **depth**.
The **thermocline** = zone of rapid temperature decrease with depth (between warm surface and cold deep water).
Factors: latitude, unequal land/water distribution, prevailing winds, ocean currents.

sections.heading: 3. Salinity of Ocean Water
points: **Salinity** = amount of dissolved salts (grams per 1000 g of water = **parts per thousand, ‰**); average ocean salinity ~**35‰**.
Salinity is affected by **evaporation, precipitation, freshwater inflow (rivers), and mixing**.
High salinity in enclosed hot seas (**Dead Sea, Lake Van** very high); low near river mouths and where rainfall is high.
Salinity generally decreases from subtropics toward equator and poles.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Oceans = ~71% of Earth's surface; Pacific = largest; Mariana Trench = deepest.
Ocean floor: continental shelf → slope → abyssal plain → trench.
Continental shelf = shallow, richest in fisheries/oil.
Thermocline = zone of rapid temperature fall with depth.
Average ocean salinity ~35‰; Dead Sea extremely saline.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **continental shelf** is the **shallowest** and richest zone (fisheries, oil).
**Salinity is measured in parts per thousand (‰)**; ocean average ~35‰.
The **thermocline** separates warm surface water from cold deep water.
